newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro shares ease ahead of U.S. jobs figures.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro shares ease ahead of U.S. jobs figures.

text.p: European shares took a few steps backwards in morning business on Friday when the enthusiasm which drove them to new records in the previous day's trading was tempered by caution ahead of a crucial set of U.S. jobs figures.
"We're not going to move out of a fairly narrow range ahead of the data," a share dealer in London said. "It's the big number of the week and it has got some people worried."

Analysts say a stronger than expected rise in U.S. jobs during February could indicate the world's leading economy was overheating and lead to higher interest rates to choke off the threat of inflation.
Higher interest rates would be bad news for share prices by making the cost of borrowing more expensive for companies and alternative investments more attractive to investors.
Any selloff in U.S. share prices, which are at record levels, would undermine European share prices, too.
Economists' forecasts for the increase in U.S. jobs, due out at 1330 GMT, range from 118,000 to 260,000 with the average around 230,000.

London's FTSE 100 index crept into record territory at the start but share prices were mixed throughout the morning and dealers said nervousness ahead of the U.S. jobs figures had restrained the market.

Around midday, the FTSE was up just 0.5 of a point at 4,399.8 but declining stocks outnumbered gainers and dealers said the market's marginal advance was led by a handful of shares, with Glaxo Wellcome, BTR and GKN in the vanguard.

Positive newspaper comment about a bundle of blue-chip annual results released on Thursday, particularly those of Glaxo, helped to stem the downward pressure, traders said. The continued liquidity of the market is also seen helping support shares.
"All the institutions still seem to be awash with cash and obviously that will be a positive factor," one dealer said.
But he added that the market's rise to record heights might prompt some nervousness and profit-taking, saying: "Some people seem to feel slightly giddy up here."
In Paris, profit-taking took French shares lower at the opening after sharp gains in the last few days and Thursday's 1.23 percent rise. Prices rallied a touch, then fell back again towards midday.

The market was well supported, however, with non-resident investors still finding Paris attractive. "They are forced to come in, the market is going up," said one trader. Company earnings were considered good, particularly those of Promodes.
The CAC-40 index was down 15.11 at 2,683.81 at 1145 GMT.
Germany's 30-share blue-chip DAX index began bourse trading sharply lower with traders in Frankfurt seeking inspiration to give direction and cure a hangover from the record run of recent days.
The DAX fell below the 3,400-point level early on and stood at 3,379.42 points, down 38.18 or 1.12 percent, at midday.
"There isn't very much going on this morning and we don't expect to go back over 3,400 points while we are waiting for U.S. data this afternoon," said a Frankfurt trader.
The dollar was slightly easier against the mark at midsession as currency markets underwent some last minute position adjustments ahead of the U.S. figures.

Economists said the balance of risks was for a stronger-than -expected rise in payrolls because February is traditionally a month where the figures come in above expectations. They predict robust numbers for both employment and hourly earnings data.

"I think it will be a strong number -- all the anecdotal evidence points that way -- and that could see the dollar make new highs above 1.7230 and maybe even 1.73," said Lee Ferridge, foreign exchange strategist at Commerzbank in London.

The dollar traded at 1.7150 marks, down from 1.7168 late on Thursday and off earlier highs. Analysts attributed the slip to profit-taking ahead of the weekend after a strong week for the dollar and in anticipation of a raft of U.S. data due out next week.
But dealers said dollar/yen was looking rather lacklustre and was unlikely to make a dramatic move. It is expected to remain in the low- to mid-121 range during the day.
The yen has been bolstered recently by continued talk of repatriation of Japanese firms' funds before the end of the Japanese fiscal year on March 31.
The lira weakened slightly to trade at 991.75 at midsession, having earlier tested its mid-rate in the European exchange rate mechanism at 990 per mark.
CURRENCIES AT 1145 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.7150 marks and 121.23 yen, compared with 1.7168 and 121.20 late on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1145 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 0.5 of a point at 4,399.8.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 15.11 points at 2,683.81.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 38.11 points at 3,379.42.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1145 GMT
Gold was fixed at $351.70 compared with London's close on Thursday of $352.20.
